data.name: Vikram
data.gender_notes: Vikram is used as a male name in hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Sanskrit vi, 'apart', + kram, 'to step' — 'valour, stride'. Its root is Sanskrit vi + kram. A classical Sanskrit term for valour. Vikram is a Sanskrit name meaning “Valour; prowess; stride”. Families who choose it generally do so for the quality the name expresses.
data.spiritual_meaning: Vikram expresses “Valour; prowess; stride”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.etymology: From the Sanskrit vi, 'apart', + kram, 'to step' — 'valour, stride'.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vikram total 29, reducing to 2. Number 2 is associated with cooperation, sensitivity and balance.

data.cultural_impact: Vikram is used in Sanskrit naming tradition with the meaning “Valour; prowess; stride”.
data.spiritual_significance: Any spiritual significance attached to Vikram is interpretive and is labelled as such.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning “Valour; prowess; stride” is the basis of any symbolism attached to Vikram; such symbolism is interpretive.

vedic_reference.note: Vikram is a name of Vishnu in Hinduism. It is mentioned in several Hindu scriptures including the Mahabharata and the Ramayana. In the Mahabharata, Vikram is the name of a king of Ujjaini. In the Ramayana, Vikram is the name of a king of Mithila and the father of Sita, who is the wife of Rama.

historical_references.reference: A classical Sanskrit term for valour.
